![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/759ebc78c794f433bba8c1f555bc68b2da52de62741711f13bd9c9156e3c485e.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-2x,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $1$ centered at $(-1,0,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-2x$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-2x \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/43e3c386086d30431405bb3fe2ca2835595641041dd7e098f9234cab8e7b225d.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{{\rho }^{2}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
